{{Short description|Chinese mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}}
{{Western name order|Wei Juncheng}}
'''Juncheng Wei''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} ({{zh|s=魏军城|link=no}}; born 1968) is a Chinese mathematician working in the area of nonlinear [[partial differential equations]], nonlinear analysis and mathematical biology. Since 1994, he has over 500 published articles in top journals, including Annals of Mathematics, Inventiones Mathematicae, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, Duke Mathematical Journal, and SIAM Review.<ref>[http://www.math.ubc.ca/~jcwei/publicationappear.html Juncheng Wei<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

Juncheng Wei lived in Hong Kong with his wife and two children, Andrew and Sophia, until August 2013.<ref>[http://www.cuhk.edu.hk/iso/research/content/pdf/juncheng-wei.pdf]</ref>

He is now a professor of mathematics and a Canada Research Chair (Tier I) at the University of British Columbia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=3072|title = Canada Research Chairs|date = 29 November 2012}}</ref> He received a Silver [[Morningside Medal]] in 2010,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.croucher.org.hk/professor-wei-juncheng | title=Professor WEI Juncheng | date=19 May 2011 }}</ref> and was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians|invited speaker]] at the 2014 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=International Mathematical Union (IMU) |website=www.mathunion.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927014538/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |archive-date=27 September 2011}}</ref> 
In 2019, Juncheng Wei was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rsc-src.ca|title = The Royal Society of Canada|date = 20 November 2019}}</ref> 
In 2020, he was awarded the [[Jeffery-Williams Prize|CMS Jeffery–Williams Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2020/2020-jw-prize|title= 2020 Jeffery-Williams Prize|accessdate=12 February 2020}}</ref> and Simons Fellow in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees|title = Simons Fellows in Mathematics|date = 19 June 2012}}</ref>
